key_findings_en: A bride and groom, along with over 30 guests, allegedly contracted norovirus from a contaminated wedding meal served at The Box House Hotel. papers.title: Molecular characterization of a rare norovirus GII.8[P8] strain detected during pediatric acute gastroenteritis surveillance in Harbin, China
papers.abstract: Norovirus is a major causative agent of pediatric acute gastroenteritis, whereas GII.8[P8] represents a rare, non-dominant genotype with limited publicly available whole-genome data. We characterized a GII.8[P8] norovirus strain, Harbin-Nov-076-2022, detected through routine surveillance of pediatric acute gastroenteritis in Harbin, China. The strain was obtained from a stool sample of a 15-month-old female patient and subjected to whole-genome sequencing using the DNBSEQ-T7 platform. Integrated analyses included phylogenetic reconstruction, amino acid entropy profiling, selection pressure assessment, homology modeling of the capsid P protein, and B-cell epitope prediction. The near-complete genome of Harbin-Nov-076-2022 is 7486 nt in length, with a GC content of 53.81%, and displays the canonical three-open-reading-frame organization of human noroviruses. The sequence was deposited in GenBank under accession number PV416744. Phylogenetic analysis assigned the strain to the GII.8[P8] lineage, with the highest nucleotide identity of 97.52% to the Thai 2018 strain GII/Hu/TH/2018/GII.8[P8]/B6213 (ACCN: OR546393). Amino acid variability was highest in the VP2 region, with three variable sites (residues 15, 122, and 229) identified among the aligned GII.8[P8] VP2 sequences, whereas selection pressure analysis indicated that the genome was largely constrained by purifying selection. Same-template P-domain modeling predicted localized sequence-associated variations in the P2 subdomain and HBGA-binding-associated surface loops, with 59 predicted B-cell epitopes. These findings expand whole-genome evidence for rare GII.8[P8] norovirus in Northeast China and provide regional genomic data for molecular surveillance, evolutionary assessment, and antigenic characterization of non-dominant norovirus genotypes.

papers.title: Viral gastroenteritis: Molecular epidemiology of human norovirus by RT-PCR at University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, Republic of Congo
papers.abstract: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses (NoV) recognized as the predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville. This study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of NoV among children presenting with AGE, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled. Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups. Eighty percent were aged ≤5 years. The overall prevalence of NoV infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. Clinically, fever was reported in 80% of cases, increased stool frequency in 86%, and dehydration was observed in all participants (100%). A significant association was observed between age and NoV genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years. However, clinical manifestations did not differ significantly between genogroups (p > 0.05). Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. Socioeconomic conditions and inadequate hygiene practices appear to play significant roles in NoV transmission.The integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures are recommended to improve prevention and control strategies. Key words: Norovirus, acute gastroenteritis, molecular epidemiology, reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), Congo.

INTRODUCTION Noroviruses (NoV) are non-enveloped, single-stranded RNA viruses belonging to the family Caliciviridae and are 2 J. Gen. Mol. Virol. recognized as the leading etiological agents of acute viral gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide (Winder et al., 2022). They are responsible for a substantial proportion of sporadic and epidemic gastroenteritis cases across all age groups and contribute significantly to morbidity and mortality, particularly among young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals (Troeger et al., 2017). Due to their low infectious dose, prolonged environmental persistence, and high transmissibility, NoV infections represent a major global public health concern (World Health Organization (WHO), 2024; Patel et al., 2009). Diarrheal diseases remain among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in children under five years of age, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Recent estimates indicate that AGE accounts for hundreds of thousands of childhood deaths annually, with the highest disease burden occurring in Africa and South Asia (Sarno et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2017). Following the widespread introduction of rotavirus vaccines, the epidemiology of viral gastroenteritis has changed considerably, with norovirus emerging as the predominant viral cause of AGE in many regions worldwide (Cates et al., 2022; Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022). In sub-Saharan Africa, norovirus infections represent an increasing public health challenge. Several studies conducted in Burkina Faso, Mozambique, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Gabon, and Cameroon have reported substantial prevalence rates among children presenting with acute diarrhea (Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022; Afework et al., 2022; Louya et al., 2019; Rönnelid et al., 2020; Tegegne et al., 2024). However, the true burden of norovirus infection in the region remains underestimated due to limited access to molecular diagnostic methods, inadequate laboratory infrastructure, weak surveillance systems, and underreporting of gastroenteritis cases. These challenges hinder accurate estimation of disease burden and the development of effective prevention and control strategies. In developing countries, poor sanitation, limited access to safe drinking water, overcrowding, and inadequate healthcare resources contribute substantially to the transmission of enteric viruses, including NoV (Rönnelid et al., 2020). In the Republic of Congo, only a limited number of studies have investigated the epidemiology of norovirus infections. A previous study conducted in Brazzaville reported a prevalence of approximately 27% among hospitalized children with acute diarrhea (Ndjangangoye et al., 2023). Nevertheless, available epidemiological data remain scarce and fragmented. In 2020, the Republic of the Congo experienced an increase in cases of acute diarrheal disease, particularly among children requiring hospital care. Globally, norovirus had already emerged as the leading viral cause of epidemic AGE following the widespread implementation of rotavirus vaccination programs. However, despite this epidemiological context, molecular epidemiological data describing circulating norovirus genogroups were unavailable in the Republic of Congo. Therefore, documenting norovirus circulation during this period represented an important public health priority and provided baseline epidemiological information for the country (Cates et al., 2022; Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022; Lopman et al., 2022). Ideally, effective surveillance systems supported by routine molecular diagnostic testing would enable continuous monitoring of circulating norovirus strains, early detection of outbreaks, and implementation of evidence-based public health interventions. However, in the Republic of the Congo, routine laboratory diagnosis of norovirus is not widely available, and epidemiological surveillance remains limited. Consequently, information regarding circulating geno- groups, transmission patterns, and associated risk factors remains insufficient. This lack of epidemiological information may have important public health implications, including delayed outbreak detection, inadequate allocation of healthcare resources, reduced effectiveness of preventive inter- ventions, and limited preparedness for future vaccine implementation programs. Strengthening local epidemio- logical evidence is therefore essential for improving disease control strategies and informing national health policies. Therefore, the present study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of norovirus among children presenting with acute gastroenteritis at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. By addressing existing knowledge gaps, this study seeks to provide valuable epidemio- logical evidence to support norovirus surveillance, prevention, and control strategies in the Republic of Congo. MATERIALS AND METHODS Ethics statement This study was approved by the Health Sciences Research Ethics Committee of the Republic of the Congo (Reference No. 286/MRSIT/IRSSA/CERSSA). Written informed consent was *Corresponding author. E-mail: anicetboumba1974@gmail.com. Author(s) agree that this article remain permanently open access under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0 International License obtained from the parents or legal guardians of all participating children before enrollment. Study population A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June 1 to November 1, 2020, in the Pediatric Emergency Department of the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo. The study population consisted of children aged between 28 days and 17 years presenting with acute gastroenteritis during the study period, regardless of their immunological status. Acute gastroenteritis was defined as the passage of three or more loose or watery stools within a 24-h period. Children younger than 28 days of age, those presenting with bloody or mucoid diarrhea, and those with chronic or prolonged gastroenteritis were excluded from the study. The inclusion of a broad pediatric age range (28 days to 17 years) was intended to provide a comprehensive assessment of norovirus circulation across the pediatric population attending the referral hospital. Although norovirus infections are more frequently reported among children under five years of age, older children may also contribute to transmission dynamics and disease burden. Sample collection Participants were recruited using a consecutive sampling strategy. All eligible children presenting during the study period were enrolled consecutively until the target sample size was reached. The sample size of 50 participants corresponded to all eligible patients recruited during the study period and reflected the logistical and financial constraints associated with molecular testing. Although relatively small, this sample provided preliminary epidemiological data on norovirus infections among children with acute gastroenteritis in Brazzaville. A structured questionnaire was administered to collect sociodemographic, environmental, and clinical information. Stool samples were collected from all enrolled participants and transported under appropriate conditions to the laboratory. Samples were stored at −80°C until molecular analysis. Molecular analyses were performed at the Molecular Biology Laboratory of the Marie Madeleine GOMBES Foundation in Pointe-Noire. RNA extraction RNA extraction was performed using the Stool Total RNA Purification Kit Dx (NORGEN BIOTEK CORPORATION, Canada), following the manufacturer's instructions. This method is designed for isolation and purification of high-quality total RNA from stool samples, and based on spin column chromatography using Norgen’s proprietary resin as the separation matrix. RNA extracts were stored at -20°C prior to NoV detection and genogroup identification. Detection of NoV RNA and genotyping by real-time PCR Detection and genogroup identification of norovirus were performed using the RealStar Norovirus reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) Kit 3.0 (Altona Diagnostics, Germany). This assay allows qualitative detection and differentiation of norovirus genogroups GI and GII. The assay differentiates genogroups GI and GII using genotype-specific primers and hydrolysis probes labeled with distinct fluorescent dyes. Detection of fluorescence in the GI channel alone was interpreted as GI infection, whereas fluorescence detected only in the GII channel indicated GII infection. Simultaneous amplification in both channels, Amona et al. 3 together with valid internal and external controls, was interpreted as a mixed GI/GII infection according to the manufacturer's instructions. Positive and negative controls provided by the manufacturer were included in each RT-PCR run to ensure assay reliability. In addition, the heterologous internal control included in the kit was used to monitor both nucleic acid extraction efficiency and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) inhibition. Amplification was carried out on a MIC qPCR thermocycler using the following thermal profile: reverse transcription at 55°C for 20 min, initial denaturation at 95°C for 2 min, followed by 45 amplification cycles consisting of denaturation at 95°C for 15 s, annealing at 55°C for 45 s, and extension at 72°C for 15 s. All molecular procedures were conducted according to established laboratory quality assurance procedures, including standardized operating protocols, equipment maintenance, contamination prevention measures, and validation of control reactions before interpretation of results. Statistical analysis Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software version 27.0.1. Categorical variables were expressed as frequencies and percentages. Associations between categorical variables were assessed using the Chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test when appropriate. Continuous variables were compared using Student’s t-test. Statistical significance was defined as a p-value < 0.05. RESULTS Socio-demographic and clinical characteristics of the study population A total of 50 children presenting with acute gastroenteritis were enrolled in this study. The majority of participants were aged ≤ 5 years (80%), while children older than 5 years represented 20% of the study population. The sex distribution was balanced, with 25 females (50%) and 25 males (50%). Regarding socioeconomic status, more than half of the participants originated from low-income households, while two-thirds were exposed to poor hygiene conditions, which is consistent with the continuing sanitation challenges reported in several low- income countries (Okesanya et al., 2024; WHO, 2025). Clinically, fever was observed in 80% of participants, increased stool frequency in 86%, and signs of dehydration were reported in all enrolled children (100%) (Table 1). Prevalence and distribution of NoV genogroups Norovirus RNA was detected in 22 of the 50 stool samples analyzed, resulting in an overall molecular prevalence of 44%. Among the positive samples, genogroup GII was the predominant circulating strain and was detected in 16 of 22 positive cases (73%). Genogroup GI was identified in 4 cases (18%), while mixed GI/GII infections were observed in 2 cases (9%), demonstrating the co-circulation of multiple norovirus 4 J. Gen. Mol. Virol. Table 1. Association between clinical manifestations and genogroups Analysis revealed a statistically significant association between age group and norovirus genogroup distribution (p = 0.03). Children aged ≤ 5 years were more frequently infected with genogroup GII compared with older children. No statistically significant association was observed between norovirus genogroups and clinical manifestations, including diarrhea, vomiting, fever, stool volume, or dehydration (p > 0.05) (Table 3). These findings suggest that although genogroup GII predominates among younger children, the clinical presentation of norovirus infection remains largely similar across circulating genogroups. DISCUSSION Acute gastroenteritis remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among children worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to healthcare, safe drinking water, and adequate sanitation remains limited. In recent years, norovirus has emerged as the leading viral cause of acute gastroenteritis following the widespread implementation of rotavirus vaccination programs (Cates et al., 2022; Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022; Lopman et al., 2022). In the present study, the molecular prevalence of norovirus infection among children presenting with acute gastroenteritis was 44%. This prevalence is higher than that previously reported in the Republic of the Congo by Louya et al. (2019) and exceeds estimates reported from neighboring African countries, including Gabon, Ethiopia, and Nigeria (Ndjangangoye et al., 2023; Manouana et al., 2021; Tegegne et al., 2024; Omosigho et al., 2025). The relatively high prevalence observed in this study may be attributed to differences in study populations, healthcare- seeking behavior, seasonal variations, environmental conditions, and the use of sensitive molecular diagnostic techniques. Furthermore, the higher prevalence may be explained by the fact that sampling was conducted during the 2020 diarrheal disease epidemic, when viral gastroenteritis activity was particularly intense. papers.title_zh: 病毒性胃肠炎:在刚果共和国布拉柴维尔大学医院中心通过 RT-PCR 检测人 流行病学 分子 流行病学
papers.source_body_en: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses (NoV) recognized as the predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville. This study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of NoV among children presenting with AGE, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled. Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups. Eighty percent were aged ≤5 years. The overall prevalence of NoV infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. Clinically, fever was reported in 80% of cases, increased stool frequency in 86%, and dehydration was observed in all participants (100%). A significant association was observed between age and NoV genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years. However, clinical manifestations did not differ significantly between genogroups (p > 0.05). Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. Socioeconomic conditions and inadequate hygiene practices appear to play significant roles in NoV transmission.The integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures are recommended to improve prevention and control strategies. Key words: Norovirus, acute gastroenteritis, molecular epidemiology, reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), Congo.

papers.title: Zymosan-adjuvanted intranasal norovirus virus-like particle vaccine induces antiviral mucosal immune responses in infant mice.
papers.abstract: Infants require repeated immunizations of injectable-type vaccines against different pathogens because their immune systems are weaker than those of adults. However, these injectable vaccines cause physical and psychological discomfort. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop pain-free mucosal vaccines that are optimized for immunologically immature infants. Using an infant murine model, we examined the effectiveness of an intranasal norovirus virus-like-particle (VLP) vaccine with zymosan as an adjuvant. The intranasal immunization of infant mice with VLPs alone induced mucosal and systemic VLP-specific immune responses that were substantially weaker than those of adults. In contrast, infant mice administered a minimum dose of intranasal zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine showed increased levels of intestinal and salivary VLP-specific IgA antibodies, as well as plasma VLP-specific IgG antibodies, at levels comparable to those in adults. Importantly, intestinal and salivary antibodies elicited by intranasal immunization with the zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine effectively inhibited norovirus propagation in human-induced pluripotent stem cellderived intestinal epithelial cells. These findings suggest that the intranasal zymosan-adjuvanted norovirus VLP vaccine is an effective mucosal vaccine candidate for infants. It may help reduce the pain associated with injections and the number of immunizations infants required to achieve sufficient protective immunity against norovirus.

papers.abstract_zh: 婴幼儿因免疫系统较成年人更为薄弱,需反复接种针剂型疫苗以预防不同病原体。然而,此类针剂型疫苗会引发生理和心理不适。因此,亟需开发适用于免疫系统发育不成熟婴幼儿的无痛黏膜型疫苗。本研究采用婴幼鼠模型,探究以酵母聚糖为佐剂的鼻喷诺如病毒病毒样颗粒(VLP)疫苗的免疫效果。单独鼻喷VLP免疫婴幼鼠仅诱导出较成年鼠显著减弱的黏膜和系统性VLP特异性免疫应答。相比之下,接种最低剂量酵母聚糖佐剂化鼻喷VLP 疫苗的婴幼鼠,其肠道和唾液中VLP特异性IgA抗体水平,以及血浆中VLP特异性IgG抗体水平,均与成年鼠相当。值得注意的是,鼻喷酵母聚糖佐剂化VLP 疫苗所诱导的肠道和唾液抗体,可有效抑制诺如病毒在人诱导多能干细胞来源肠上皮细胞中的增殖。研究结果表明,鼻喷酵母聚糖佐剂化诺如病毒 VLP 疫苗是一种有效的婴幼儿黏膜型疫苗候选制剂,有望减轻注射带来的疼痛并降低婴幼儿为达到足够保护性免疫所需的接种次数。

papers.title: Norovirus on Cruise Ships: A Recurring Sentinel Event
papers.abstract: Norovirus remains the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis outbreaks worldwide and is particularly well adapted for transmission aboard cruise ships due to its low infectious dose, prolonged environmental persistence, and rapid person-to-person spread. We reviewed recent outbreaks to highlight recurring norovirus outbreaks and gaps in maritime surveillance. These demonstrate the vulnerability of cruise ships to rapid viral amplification and international dissemination. Current surveillance relies predominantly on symptomatic case reporting, limiting the ability to distinguish between single-source introduction, environmental persistence, foodborne transmission, and emergence of novel recombinant strains. Recent modelling studies have shown that early diagnosis and isolation of symptomatic individuals substantially reduce secondary transmission, yet routine genomic surveillance is rarely implemented onboard. Wastewater-based surveillance offers a practical, non-invasive early warning approach that can be integrated into existing ship infrastructure and complemented by genomic sequencing to identify circulating variants and transmission pathways. Incorporating molecular and wastewater surveillance into routine maritime health programmes would strengthen outbreak detection, improve infection control, and enhance global preparedness for recurrent norovirus outbreaks associated with international cruise travel.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on norovirus as the primary pathogen causing acute gastroenteritis outbreaks on cruise ships. The study highlights the virus's adaptability to maritime environments due to its low infectious dose, environmental persistence, and rapid spread. The evidence base includes recent outbreaks and modeling studies, which emphasize the need for improved surveillance and infection control measures. Current methods rely heavily on symptomatic reporting, which limits the ability to differentiate transmission routes. The review underscores the importance of integrating wastewater-based and genomic surveillance to enhance outbreak detection and control. Despite the potential benefits of early diagnosis and isolation, genomic surveillance is not routinely implemented on cruise ships. The findings suggest that strengthening surveillance systems and infection control protocols could improve global preparedness for norovirus outbreaks associated with international travel.

media_mentions.content: Abstract Norovirus remains the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis outbreaks worldwide and is particularly well adapted for transmission aboard cruise ships due to its low infectious dose, prolonged environmental persistence, and rapid person-to-person spread. We reviewed recent outbreaks to highlight recurring norovirus outbreaks and gaps in maritime surveillance. These demonstrate the vulnerability of cruise ships to rapid viral amplification and international dissemination. Current surveillance relies predominantly on symptomatic case reporting, limiting the ability to distinguish between single-source introduction, environmental persistence, foodborne transmission, and emergence of novel recombinant strains. Recent modelling studies have shown that early diagnosis and isolation of symptomatic individuals substantially reduce secondary transmission, yet routine genomic surveillance is rarely implemented onboard. Wastewater-based surveillance offers a practical, non-invasive early warning approach that can be integrated into existing ship infrastructure and complemented by genomic sequencing to identify circulating variants and transmission pathways. Incorporating molecular and wastewater surveillance into routine maritime health programmes would strengthen outbreak detection, improve infection control, and enhance global preparedness for recurrent norovirus outbreaks associated with international cruise travel. Editorial In 2026, three significant norovirus outbreaks were reported aboard the Star Princess, Caribbean Princess, and Ambition between March and May 2026 [1-3]. However, despite recurrent outbreaks, cruise ships continue to be potent amplification environments for norovirus transmission. However, genomic surveillance and outbreak tracking remain restricted [4,5]. This indicates a persistent gap in global maritime infectious disease surveillance, highlighting this continuing public health challenge. The outbreaks on the three cruise ships highlight how quickly enteric viruses like norovirus can disseminate across international travel networks once introduced into confined maritime settings (Table 1, Figure 1). During a seven-day voyage (March 7-14, 2026), the Star Princess recorded 193 cases of gastrointestinal illness among 5,868 passengers and crew, with a 3.29% attack rate. The United States Vessel Sanitation Program was notified on March 11, 2026 [1]. The Caribbean Princess, which departed Port Everglades on April 28, 2026, reported 160 cases of gastrointestinal illness during its 13-day Southern Caribbean voyage among 4,247 passengers and crew, corresponding to a 3.77% attack rate [2]. The Ambition, operated by Ambassador Cruise Line, departed Belfast on May 8, 2026, for a 14-night voyage to France and Spain. The vessel carried 1,187 passengers and 514 crew members (1,701 total). After arriving in Bordeaux, French authorities temporarily restricted disembarkation because of an outbreak of gastrointestinal illness. As of May 14, 2026, 60 passengers and four crew members were reported to be experiencing gastrointestinal illness, and laboratory testing confirmed norovirus [3]. Norovirus is uniquely adapted for transmission aboard cruise ships. Its very low infectious dose, prolonged environmental persistence, resistance to commonly used disinfectants, and efficient aerosolisation during vomiting make it particularly suited to cruise ship environments [2,5]. Hundreds of passengers share ventilation systems, dining halls, recreational facilities, and semi-enclosed cabin corridors for prolonged periods. The CDC Vessel Sanitation Program continues to document recurrent gastrointestinal illness outbreaks aboard cruise ships, with norovirus identified as the causative agent in many reported events [6]. Regular handwashing, thorough cooking of shellfish, proper washing of fresh produce, and disinfection of contaminated surfaces are recommended preventive measures against norovirus [6]. Recent modelling studies further highlight the importance of early case identification and isolation during norovirus outbreaks aboard cruise ships. Analysis of seven Mediterranean cruise outbreaks involving 359 cases demonstrated that isolation of diagnosed individuals immediately upon symptoms reduced their transmissibility by approximately 94% under the study conditions. The same modelling framework improved forecasts compared with a baseline model, with improvement observed for 78% of data points at forecasting horizons longer than 72 hours [7]. These findings support rapid diagnosis and cabin isolation as important outbreak-control measures while also illustrating how mathematical modelling can complement routine syndromic surveillance. There are still significant gaps in outbreak surveillance. Most cruise ships continue to rely primarily on symptomatic passengers reporting to onboard medical services, a strategy that frequently detects outbreaks only after substantial transmission has already occurred [8]. Routine sequencing of norovirus strains is rarely performed onboard, making it difficult to distinguish between single-source introduction, ongoing environmental contamination, foodborne transmission, and the emergence of novel recombinant variants. Genomic surveillance could additionally help track inter-voyage viral spread across ports and identify globally circulating strains associated with repeated maritime outbreaks [5]. This limitation has important public health implications. During outbreaks at sea, clinicians cannot readily determine whether cases result from a single introduction, ongoing environmental contamination, foodborne transmission, or the emergence of a new variant. Syndromic surveillance alone is insufficient to distinguish between these scenarios, although each requires different public health interventions [4,5,8]. Wastewater-based surveillance offers a practical solution. It requires no active passenger participation, can be integrated into existing ship infrastructure, and has already proven valuable as an early-warning tool during the COVID-19 pandemic. Wastewater surveillance could serve as a complementary, non-invasive early-warning approach on cruise ships and could be paired with genomic sequencing to characterize circulating norovirus strains. Passive wastewater sampling has been explored as a scalable infectious-disease surveillance strategy, including during the COVID-19 pandemic [9]. Such an approach could enable earlier detection while complementing, rather than replacing, clinical surveillance. Despite growing global attention to marine health security, these approaches remain largely absent from routine cruise ship operations. Integrating syndromic surveillance with targeted wastewater-based molecular detection and genomic sequencing could provide a more comprehensive approach to maritime infectious-disease surveillance. The objective should not be to create an entirely new surveillance system onboard every vessel, but to complement existing medical reporting and sanitation systems with targeted molecular surveillance that is feasible, scalable, and linked to established public health response pathways. Such integration could facilitate earlier recognition of outbreaks, improve understanding of transmission, and strengthen preparedness for recurrent norovirus events associated with international cruise travel. papers.title: Treatment With Ruxolitinib and TAK-779 Enhances GII.17 Human Norovirus Replication and Enables Serial Passaging in Human Intestinal Enteroids.
papers.abstract: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis. Although it can be replicated in vitro using human intestinal enteroids (HIEs), generating high-titer viral laboratory stocks remains challenging due to low infection and passage efficiencies. Interferon response and chemokine signaling may be key host pathways that restrict efficient HuNoV replication. Here, we evaluated the effect of their inhibitors, ruxolitinib-a Janus kinase (JAK) 1/JAK2 inhibitor-and TAK-779-a C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)/C-C motif chemokine receptor (CCR) 5/CCR2 antagonist-on HuNoV replication in wild-type jejunal HIEs. TAK-779 increased GII.17 HuNoV replication by 2.3- and 6.0-fold at 48 and 96 h postinfection (hpi), respectively, compared with the DMSO-treated control. In contrast, ruxolitinib alone did not affect viral replication. Notably, simultaneous treatment with these compounds further enhanced GII.17 replication by 6.0- and 10.7-fold at 48 and 96 hpi, respectively, which enabled serial passaging. These findings imply that the simultaneous suppression of these pathways potentially benefits GII.17 HuNoV replication.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of ruxolitinib and TAK-779 on GII.17 human norovirus (HuNoV) replication in human intestinal enteroids (HIEs). The research aimed to address the challenge of generating high-titer viral stocks due to low replication efficiency. The results showed that TAK-779 significantly increased viral replication at 48 and 96 hpi, while ruxolitinib alone had no effect. Simultaneous treatment with both compounds led to a further enhancement, enabling serial passaging. These findings suggest that targeting interferon response and chemokine signaling pathways could improve HuNoV replication in vitro. The study provides insights into potential therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections but has limited implications for broader applications due to its focus on a specific viral genotype and in vitro model.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics associated with gastrointestinal bleeding in neonates with laboratory-confirmed norovirus gastroenteritis
papers.abstract: Introduction Norovirus (NoV) is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis in children, but pathogen-confirmed data in neonates remain limited, particularly regarding clinical differences associated with gastrointestinal bleeding. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study of neonates younger than 28 days who were hospitalized at the Children's Hospital of Soochow University between December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2025, had positive stool NoV antigen results, and underwent confirmatory nucleic acid testing. After excluding clinically identifiable alternative causes of gastrointestinal bleeding, patients were classified into hemorrhagic and non-hemorrhagic groups. Baseline characteristics, clinical manifestations, comorbidities, and laboratory findings obtained within 24 h after admission were compared between groups. Laboratory variables showing significant between-group differences were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model. Results A total of 139 neonates were included, comprising 52 in the hemorrhagic group and 87 in the non-hemorrhagic group. Among the hemorrhagic cases, 49 had overt gastrointestinal bleeding and three had isolated fecal occult blood positivity. The hemorrhagic group had a higher frequency of diarrhea and a lower frequency of jaundice. Hemoglobin, total bilirubin, indirect bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase, the aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase ratio, pH-corrected venous ionized calcium, chloride, and lactate were lower in the hemorrhagic group, whereas blood base excess was higher. In multivariable logistic regression, each 0.1 mmol/L increase in ionized calcium was associated with lower odds of the hemorrhagic phenotype (OR = 0.624, 95% CI: 0.410–0.950; P = 0.028). Discussion Neonates with laboratory-confirmed NoV gastroenteritis showed different clinical and laboratory characteristics according to the presence of gastrointestinal bleeding. The association with lower ionized calcium should be interpreted cautiously because of the retrospective design and potential residual confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated clinical characteristics associated with gastrointestinal bleeding in neonates with laboratory-confirmed norovirus gastroenteritis. A single-center retrospective observational study was conducted on 139 neonates hospitalized between December 31, 2024, and December 31, 2025, at the Children's Hospital of Soochow University. Neonates were classified into hemorrhagic and non-hemorrhagic groups after excluding alternative causes of bleeding. Baseline characteristics, clinical manifestations, comorbidities, and laboratory findings were compared between groups. The hemorrhagic group showed a higher frequency of diarrhea and lower levels of hemoglobin, total bilirubin, and ionized calcium, along with higher blood base excess. A multivariable logistic regression model found that each 0.1 mmol/L increase in ionized calcium was associated with lower odds of the hemorrhagic phenotype. The study highlights potential clinical and laboratory markers for gastrointestinal bleeding in neonates with norovirus infection, which could aid in targeted surveillance and management. However, the retrospective design and potential residual confounding limit the strength of the findings.

papers.full_text: Abstract Wastewater-based surveillance is a recent, innovative strategy for tracking enteric virus circulation, thus providing early warning of infectious disease outbreaks. However, actual wastewater monitoring is limited by the lack of rapid, portable, and contamination-resistant molecular assays suitable for decentralized applications. Preventing amplicon aerosol contamination while maintaining high analytical sensitivity remains also a major challenge for nucleic acid detection based on clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) in environmental samples. We developed a fully closed recombinase polymerase amplification combined with CRISPR-associated protein 13a lateral flow assay for contamination-free detection of norovirus and rotavirus in wastewater. The platform was evaluated using synthetic ribonucleic acid standards and validated with 28 wastewater samples collected from a municipal wastewater treatment plant in China over 12 months, with each sample analyzed for both viruses. The closed reaction system integrated isothermal amplification, the collateral cleavage activity of the clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats-associated protein 13a, and gold nanoparticle-based lateral flow detection within a sealed reaction vessel. Performance was assessed by analytical sensitivity, specificity, and agreement with quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Results show that the optimized assay achieved a limit of detection of 1 attomolar in approximately 90 min, showed no cross-reactivity with tested non-target viruses. Analysis of the two target viruses in 28 wastewater samples generated 56 virus-specific test results, with 14 positive detections, comparable to quantitative polymerase chain reaction. These findings demonstrate ultrasensitive, contamination-free virus detection and provide a portable platform for wastewater-based epidemiology and on-site public health surveillance. papers.title_original: A contamination-free lateral flow platform for point-of-care virus detection in wastewater

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of current wastewater monitoring by developing a contamination-free detection platform for norovirus and rotavirus, which are key enteric viruses of public health concern. The background highlights the need for rapid, portable, and contamination-resistant molecular assays for decentralized wastewater-based surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the development and validation of a closed reaction system for detecting norovirus and rotavirus in wastewater samples collected from a municipal treatment plant in China over 12 months. The platform was tested on 28 wastewater samples, with each sample analyzed for both target viruses.
analysis.methods: The platform utilized recombinase polymerase amplification combined with CRISPR-associated protein 13a lateral flow assay. Performance was evaluated through analytical sensitivity, specificity, and agreement with quantitative polymerase chain reaction.
analysis.main_results: The optimized assay achieved a limit of detection of 1 attomolar in approximately 90 minutes and showed no cross-reactivity with tested non-target viruses. Analysis of the two target viruses in 28 wastewater samples generated 56 virus-specific test results, with 14 positive detections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate the platform's ability to provide ultrasensitive, contamination-free virus detection, which is a novel approach for wastewater-based epidemiology and on-site public health surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The platform offers a portable solution for wastewater-based surveillance, which can enhance early warning systems for infectious disease outbreaks and support real-time public health monitoring.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited to synthetic RNA standards and 28 wastewater samples, which may affect generalizability. However, the results are consistent with quantitative polymerase chain reaction, suggesting moderate confidence in the platform's performance.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a contamination-free lateral flow platform for detecting norovirus and rotavirus in wastewater. The platform combines recombinase polymerase amplification with CRISPR-associated protein 13a and gold nanoparticle-based detection. It was validated using synthetic RNA standards and 28 wastewater samples from a Chinese treatment plant over 12 months, achieving a limit of detection of 1 attomolar in about 90 minutes. The results showed no cross-reactivity with non-target viruses and 14 positive detections across 56 tests, comparable to quantitative polymerase chain reaction. The findings highlight the platform's potential for enhancing wastewater-based epidemiology and public health surveillance. However, the study's limited sample size and reliance on synthetic standards may affect generalizability, resulting in moderate confidence in the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过开发一种无污染检测平台,解决当前废水监测的局限性,该平台针对轮状病毒和另一种肠道病毒(轮状病毒为公共卫生关注的关键肠道病毒)。背景强调了对适用于分散废水基监测的快速、便携且抗污染分子检测方法的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究开发并验证了一种封闭反应系统,用于在中国某市政污水处理厂收集的废水样本中检测轮状病毒和另一种肠道病毒,收集期为12个月。该平台在28份废水样本上进行了测试,每份样本均检测两种靶标病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 该平台采用重组聚合酶扩增与CRISPR相关蛋白13a侧向流检测技术。通过分析灵敏度、特异性及与定量聚合酶链反应(qPCR)的符合性评估其性能。
elements_zh.main_results: 优化后的检测方法在约90分钟内实现了1阿托摩尔的检测限,且与测试的非靶标病毒无交叉反应。在28份废水样本中对两种靶标病毒进行分析,共产生56个病毒特异性检测结果,其中14个为阳性检测。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证明该平台具备超灵敏、无污染的病毒检测能力,这是废水基监测和现场公共卫生监测的一种新颖方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该平台为废水基监测提供便携式解决方案,可增强传染病预警系统,并支持实时公共卫生监测。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的证据仅限于合成RNA标准品和28份废水样本,可能影响结果的普遍性。然而,结果与定量聚合酶链反应(qPCR)一致,表明该平台性能具有中等可信度。

papers.title: Emergence of a novel GII.17 variant is associated with immune evasion rather than an altered HBGA-binding profile
papers.abstract: The epidemiology of noroviruses, a major cause of gastroenteritis in humans, is shaped by their continuous evolution. Novel genotypes and variants periodically emerge, replacing previously dominant strains. In 2024, a novel GII.17 variant led to an increased number of notified outbreaks, becoming the dominant genotype detected in Europe. To investigate if this surge in GII.17 detection is attributable to changes in binding and antigenicity of this novel variant, we compared properties of a GII.17 2024 strain with representative GII.17 strains from 2005 (Clade B), 2014 (Clade C), and 2015 (Clade D), and the epidemic GII.4 Sydney 2012 variant. Norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) were used to assess binding to saliva samples and human intestinal tissues with different histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) profiles. Binding specificity to individual glycans was determined using synthetic HBGAs. Additionally, VP1-NanoLuc (NLuc) fusion proteins were used in binding blocking assays to evaluate the antigenic properties of the variants using 75 sera from healthy adults that were collected during different time periods of GII.17 circulation (the winters of 2009–2010, 2015 and 2024). Compared with other GII.17 variants, the 2024 strain exhibits amino acid substitutions in the P2 domain, which contains both antigenic sites and the HBGA binding site. Binding-blocking assays with human sera confirmed that the 2024 variant is antigenically distinct from the 2005 and 2015 GII.17 strains but closely related to the 2014 variant. All post-2005 GII.17 strains showed a broader HBGA binding profile compared to the GII.17 2005 strain, likely contributing to their more successful spread. These findings show that the recent re-emergence of GII.17 coincided with antigenic drift, enabling it to escape from pre-existing immunity, but not with major changes in HBGA binding specificity. Understanding the factors influencing norovirus emergence is essential for the development of preventive strategies against future norovirus epidemics.

papers.title: Breastfeeding and viral infections in preterm infants: a multicenter cohort study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of breastfeeding status up to 6 months of age on the incidence of viral infections during the first year of life in preterm infants. METHODS: Data were obtained from the Japanese National Hospital Organization Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Registry for the periods 2010-2014 and 2016-2018. Information on breastfeeding exposure and infection history was collected through parental questionnaires administered when the infants reached one year of age. A total of 3,368 preterm infants who completed follow-up at one year were analyzed. The risk ratio (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using a modified Poisson regression model to evaluate the association between breastfeeding and the risk of viral infections, including influenza virus, respiratory syncytial (RS) virus, rotavirus, and norovirus. RESULTS: Breastfeeding was associated with a lower risk of influenza infection (adjusted RR: 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.89) and indicated a trend toward lower risk for other viral infections. CONCLUSION: Breastfeeding for up to 6 months may lower the risk of viral infections in preterm infants, suggesting that providing breastfeeding support could contribute to improved health outcomes. IMPACT: This study examined the association between breastfeeding up to 6 months and viral infections in preterm infants using data from a multicenter cohort. Breastfeeding was associated with a lower incidence of influenza and showed a possible protective association with other viral infections. These findings support the promotion of breastfeeding in preterm infants as part of infection prevention strategies. Given the vulnerability of preterm infants, further research is required to confirm these associations and to evaluate the long-term health implications of breastfeeding.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of breastfeeding on viral infections in preterm infants, focusing on norovirus and other related viruses. It used a multicenter cohort design, collecting data from the Japanese National Hospital Organization Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Registry between 2010-2014 and 2016-2018. Parental questionnaires were used to gather information on breastfeeding exposure and infection history, with 3,368 preterm infants included in the analysis. The study found that breastfeeding was associated with a lower risk of influenza infection and showed a trend toward lower risk for other viral infections, including norovirus. The authors suggest that breastfeeding support may improve health outcomes in preterm infants. However, they note the need for further research to confirm these associations and assess long-term implications. The evidence is moderate, as the study relies on self-reported data and does not account for all potential confounding factors.

papers.title: Microbial assessment of recontamination with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter in patient room environment in a burn unit.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Numerous studies have demonstrated that environmental contamination with several epidemiologically important pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus spp, Acinetobacter, norovirus, and Clostridioides difficile, can persist for several days to months and contributes to the transmission of these pathogens. METHODS: This study was conducted in a burn intensive care unit to determine the time to recontamination of environmental surfaces with a multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection. After disinfection, samples were taken from 6 environmental sites using Rodac plates at 1-hour intervals for 10 hours. RESULTS: Time to recontamination with Acinetobacter was as follows: chair, 3 hours; overbed table, 2 hours; stock cabinet, 3 hours; and IV pump, 2 hours. CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrated that recontamination with Acinetobacter occurred rapidly at environmental sites in burn units even after cleaning/disinfection and underscored the need for enhanced environmental cleaning, including continuous disinfection methods, to prevent transmission of health care-associated pathogens.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the persistent problem of environmental contamination by epidemiologically important pathogens in healthcare settings and sought to determine how quickly surfaces become recontaminated with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective observational study was conducted in a burn intensive care unit to measure the time to recontamination of environmental surfaces with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after routine disinfection.
analysis.methods: Environmental samples were collected from six specific sites using Rodac plates at 1-hour intervals for 10 hours following disinfection to assess recontamination dynamics.
analysis.main_results: Recontamination with Acinetobacter occurred rapidly, with positive samples detected at 2 hours on the overbed table and IV pump, and at 3 hours on the chair and stock cabinet.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that recontamination happens quickly even after cleaning, highlighting the need for enhanced environmental cleaning strategies, including continuous disinfection, to reduce transmission risks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the importance of implementing more rigorous and continuous disinfection protocols in burn units to prevent healthcare-associated Acinetobacter transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a single burn unit and did not evaluate the effectiveness of specific disinfection methods or long-term outcomes, indicating moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study in a burn intensive care unit assessed how quickly environmental surfaces become recontaminated with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection. Sampling from six sites using Rodac plates at hourly intervals for 10 hours showed that recontamination occurred within 2 to 3 hours, with positive samples detected earliest on the overbed table and IV pump. The authors interpreted these results as evidence that routine cleaning is insufficient and that continuous disinfection is necessary to reduce transmission risks. The findings suggest that enhanced environmental cleaning protocols are urgently needed in burn units to prevent healthcare-associated Acinetobacter infections.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:大量研究表明,环境中多种流行病学重要病原体的污染,包括耐甲氧西林金黄色葡萄球菌、耐万古霉素肠球菌、不动杆菌、诺如病毒和艰难梭菌,可以持续数天至数月,并导致这些病原体的传播。方法:本研究在烧伤重症监护室进行,以确定消毒后环境表面被多重耐药鲍曼不动杆菌再次污染的时间。消毒后,使用Rodac板在6个环境点采样10小时,每隔1小时采样一次。结果:不动杆菌再次污染的时间如下:椅子,3小时;床头柜,2小时;库存柜,3小时;和 IV 泵,2 小时。结论:我们的研究表明,即使在清洁/消毒后,不动杆菌的再污染也会在烧伤单位的环境部位迅速发生,并强调需要加强环境清洁,包括持续消毒方法,以防止医疗保健相关病原体的 传播。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究针对医疗环境中流行病学重要病原体对环境污染的持续问题,旨在确定环境表面在消毒后多久会被多重耐药鲍曼不动杆菌(Acinetobacter baumannii)再次污染。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项前瞻性观察研究,在烧伤重症监护室(ICU)中进行,用于测量环境表面在常规消毒后被多重耐药鲍曼不动杆菌再次污染所需的时间。
analysis_zh.methods: 在消毒后的10小时内,每隔1小时从六个特定位点采集环境样本,使用Rodac平板进行培养,以评估再污染动态。
analysis_zh.main_results: 再污染发生迅速,消毒后2小时在床头桌和静脉输液泵上检测到鲍曼不动杆菌阳性样本,3小时在椅子和储物柜上检测到。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论:即使经过清洁,再污染也会迅速发生,这凸显了需要加强环境清洁策略,包括持续消毒,以减少传播风险。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了在烧伤病房实施更严格且持续消毒方案的重要性,以预防医院获得性鲍曼不动杆菌传播。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单一烧伤病房,未评估特定消毒方法的有效性或长期结局,表明证据强度为中等。

papers.title: Evolution, diversity and distribution of human Noroviruses:From single hosts to global patterns
papers.abstract: Norovirus, a member of the Caliciviridae family, is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, affecting all age groups and causing substantial morbidity and mortality. Children in developing countries, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals are particularly affected. Currently, no specific antivirals or vaccines are licensed for norovirus treatment or prevention. Therapeutic development is complicated by the virus's high diversity, with more than 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, some of which, such as GII.4, continuously generate new antigenic variants. However, the emergence of norovirus diversity, the relationship between within-host and community-level evolution, and the association between viral diversity and treatment outcome remain incompletely understood. Therefore, this thesis aims to improve our understanding of norovirus evolution and epidemiology by addressing two main topics: norovirus diversity and evolution in different hosts, and the use of wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus causes substantial global morbidity and mortality from acute gastroenteritis, yet key knowledge gaps persist regarding its high diversity, within-host and community-level evolution, and links between diversity and treatment outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This thesis synthesizes existing evidence to address norovirus diversity and epidemiology across hosts and populations, integrating host-specific analyses and wastewater-based sequencing for population-level monitoring.
analysis.methods: The study employs a comparative and integrative approach, combining literature review with wastewater-based sequencing to examine viral diversity and circulation patterns at the population level.
analysis.main_results: The thesis identifies over 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, with GII.4 continuously generating new antigenic variants, highlighting the virus's extensive diversity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The work interprets the observed diversity as a driver of therapeutic challenges and proposes wastewater-based sequencing as a tool to monitor norovirus evolution and circulation, emphasizing the need to bridge within-host and community-level evolutionary insights.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance strategies and underscore the urgency for vaccine and antiviral development, given the absence of licensed options and the virus's antigenic variability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by its reliance on a literature-based synthesis and wastewater sequencing, which may not capture all host-specific dynamics or treatment associations, warranting moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This thesis examines norovirus diversity and epidemiology to address critical gaps in understanding its evolution and public health impact. It synthesizes evidence showing norovirus as a major global cause of acute gastroenteritis, with over 10 genogroups and 50 genotypes, including the antigenically variable GII.4. The study integrates host-specific analyses and wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level. Key findings highlight the virus's extensive diversity as a barrier to therapeutic and vaccine development, with no licensed antivirals or vaccines currently available. The work interprets these patterns as evidence of ongoing antigenic drift and calls for improved surveillance and intervention strategies. Limitations include the reliance on literature synthesis and wastewater data, which may not fully capture host-specific dynamics or treatment outcomes, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 诺如病毒 导致大量全球发病率和 急性胃肠炎 带来的 死亡率,但在其高度多样性、宿主 内和社区层面的 进化 以及多样性与 治疗 结果之间的联系方面,关键的知识差距仍然存在。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本论文综合了现有证据来解决 宿主 和人群中的 诺如病毒 多样性和 流行病学 问题,整合了 宿主 特定分析和基于废水的测序以进行人群水平监测。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用比较和综合方法,将文献综述与基于废水的测序相结合,以检查人群水平上的病毒多样性和传播模式。
elements_zh.main_results: 该论文鉴定了超过 10 个基因组 (GI–GX) 和大约 50 个基因型,其中 GII.4 不断产生新的抗原变体,凸显了该病毒的广泛多样性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这项工作将观察到的多样性解释为治疗挑战的驱动因素,并提出基于废水的测序作为监测 诺如病毒 进化 和循环的工具,强调需要在 宿主 和群落层面的进化见解之间架起桥梁。

papers.source_body_en: Norovirus, a member of the Caliciviridae family, is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, affecting all age groups and causing substantial morbidity and mortality. Children in developing countries, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals are particularly affected. Currently, no specific antivirals or vaccines are licensed for norovirus treatment or prevention. Therapeutic development is complicated by the virus's high diversity, with more than 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, some of which, such as GII.4, continuously generate new antigenic variants. However, the emergence of norovirus diversity, the relationship between within-host and community-level evolution, and the association between viral diversity and treatment outcome remain incompletely understood. Therefore, this thesis aims to improve our understanding of norovirus evolution and epidemiology by addressing two main topics: norovirus diversity and evolution in different hosts, and the use of wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level.

papers.title: An Ultrasensitive Electrochemical Biosensor for Nucleic Acid Detection Based on Silver Nanoflower-Stem-Loop Probes
papers.abstract: Nucleic acids are critical biomarkers that provide essential information throughout disease progression, making their detection critical to early diagnosis of both infectious and non-infectious diseases. However, existing detection methods, including classical analytical techniques and even most reported biosensors, are often constrained by complex procedures, high costs, and limited sensitivity, with the majority operating at the femtomolar level and failing to achieve single-molecule detection needed for early-stage diagnosis. Here, we report an electrochemical biosensor based on silver nanoflowers (AgNFs) integrated with stem-loop probes (SPs) for universal nucleic acid detection, using Norovirus RNA as a model target to validate the platform. The SPs serve as critical elements in a signal amplification system, converting target binding into a biotin–streptavidin recognition event, which leads to the accumulation of AgNFs-SP complexes on laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrodes and generates a strong electrochemical signal. Under optimized conditions with a 50 min hybridization incubation (total assay time ~60 min), the sensor exhibits a linear response to Norovirus RNA concentrations from 1 aM to 10 fM, with a measured detection limit of 1 aM, achieving single-molecule-level detection capability. For applications requiring faster turnaround, a 20 min hybridization incubation (~30 min total assay time) shifts the linear range to 0.1 fM–1 pM with a measured detection limit of 0.1 fM, offering more rapid quantification when the maximum sensitivity is not required. The proposed biosensor is cost-effective, amenable to miniaturization, and designed as a versatile platform adaptable to other nucleic acid targets by simply modifying the probe sequence, showing broad potential for early diagnosis of various diseases.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 核酸是疾病进展的关键生物标志物,但现有检测方法在早期诊断方面灵敏度和实用性不足。本研究旨在开发一种通用的超灵敏核酸检测平台,以解决这些局限性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究设计了一种基于银纳米花与发夹探针的电化学生物传感器,并以诺如病毒 RNA为模型靶标进行验证。该平台被设计为可通过简单修改探针序列适配其他核酸靶标的通用系统。
analysis_zh.methods: 在优化条件下,杂交孵育时间为50分钟(总检测时间约60分钟)时,传感器对诺如病毒 RNA浓度在1 aM至10 fM范围内呈线性响应,检测限为1 aM。采用更快速方案,杂交孵育时间缩短至20分钟(总检测时间约30分钟)时,线性范围转移至0.1 fM–1 pM,检测限为0.1 fM。

papers.title: Living with Primary Immunodeficiencies: CVID—Enteropathy from the Perspective of a Gastroenterologist
papers.abstract: Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), the most prevalent symptomatic primary antibody deficiency (∼1:25,000), in its symptomatic spectrum reaches way beyond intractable, chronic, and recurrent infections. Noninfectious enteropathy (CVID-E)—affecting 15–30% of patients—has emerged as a pivotal manifestation of the natural disease trajectory, with approximately 11-fold increased mortality risk. CVID-E is pathologically determined by villous atrophy, absent mucosal plasma cells, and abundant CD8+ T cell infiltration—yielding the phenotype that often mimics celiac disease. There are three pathogenic determinants that have been elucidated so far. First, almost absent mucosal IgA is permeating and facilitating gut pathogen expansion. With this process, gut membrane lipid metabolism is shifted toward inflammatory cascades, which may render an inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-like phenotype. Second, a mixed and specific type I/III and type II interferon release drives CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity and macrophage recruitment, producing a graft-versus-host-like mucosal damage pattern yielding apparent villous injury. Third, chronic norovirus infection further augments this interferon-driven pathway, leading to high-grade epithelial damage even in early-onset disease. USIDNET registry analysis (n = 1,415) confirmed that CVID-E patients exhibit significantly lower performance status, higher rates of concomitant autoimmunity (30.7%), granulomatous disease, and even malignancy. Treatment is largely empirical with limited evidence-based data. Immunoglobulin replacement does not mitigate symptoms of enteropathy, and although corticosteroids restore architecture, they impose prohibitive infectious risk. Although TNF-α blockers and thiopurines achieved complete remission in select patient cohorts, overall therapeutic response was unsatisfying. Molecular medical tactics—employing JAK inhibitors targeting the interferon-specific pathways, namely abatacept for CTLA-4-related dysregulation—represent the most promising tool. CVID-E is a complicated disorder because it stands at the very intersection of immunodeficiency, immune dysregulation, and mucosal pathology where these determinants encompass collapsed humoral defense, gut dysbiosis, and unbalanced interferon-driven epithelial necrosis converge. Multicenter randomized controlled trials and precision therapeutics are urgently needed to supersede the current empirical interventions with a fully evidence-based approach.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: USIDNET registry analysis (n = 1,415) confirmed that CVID-E patients exhibit significantly lower performance status, higher rates of concomitant autoimmunity (30.7%), granulomatous disease, and even malignancy. Multicenter randomized controlled trials and precision therapeutics are urgently needed to supersede the current empirical interventions with a fully evidence-based approach.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CVID-E is pathologically determined by villous atrophy, absent mucosal plasma cells, and abundant CD8+ T cell infiltration—yielding the phenotype that often mimics celiac disease. There are three pathogenic determinants that have been elucidated so far. First, almost absent mucosal IgA is permeating and facilitating gut pathogen expansion. With this process, gut membrane lipid metabolism is shifted toward inflammatory cascades, which may render an inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-like phenotype. Second, a mixed and specific type I/III and type II interferon release drives CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity and macrophage recruitment, producing a graft-versus-host-like mucosal damage pattern yielding apparent villous injury.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Immunoglobulin replacement does not mitigate symptoms of enteropathy, and although corticosteroids restore architecture, they impose prohibitive infectious risk. Although TNF-α blockers and thiopurines achieved complete remission in select patient cohorts, overall therapeutic response was unsatisfying. Treatment is largely empirical with limited evidence-based data.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Molecular medical tactics—employing JAK inhibitors targeting the interferon-specific pathways, namely abatacept for CTLA-4-related dysregulation—represent the most promising tool. CVID-E is a complicated disorder because it stands at the very intersection of immunodeficiency, immune dysregulation, and mucosal pathology where these determinants encompass collapsed humoral defense, gut dysbiosis, and unbalanced interferon-driven epithelial necrosis converge.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of norovirus in the pathogenesis of CVID-E, a noninfectious enteropathy associated with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID). CVID-E is characterized by villous atrophy, absent mucosal plasma cells, and CD8+ T cell infiltration, often mimicking celiac disease. The review highlights three pathogenic determinants: mucosal IgA deficiency leading to gut pathogen expansion, interferon-driven immune responses causing mucosal damage, and chronic norovirus infection exacerbating these pathways. Despite the potential of JAK inhibitors and abatacept, current treatments remain empirical with limited evidence-based data. The review emphasizes the need for multicenter randomized controlled trials and precision therapeutics to address the complexities of CVID-E, which involves immunodeficiency, immune dysregulation, and mucosal pathology.

papers.title_zh: 与原发性免疫缺陷共存:CVID—从胃肠病学家视角看肠病
papers.source_body_en: Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), the most prevalent symptomatic primary antibody deficiency (∼1:25,000), in its symptomatic spectrum reaches way beyond intractable, chronic, and recurrent infections. Noninfectious enteropathy (CVID-E)—affecting 15–30% of patients—has emerged as a pivotal manifestation of the natural disease trajectory, with approximately 11-fold increased mortality risk. CVID-E is pathologically determined by villous atrophy, absent mucosal plasma cells, and abundant CD8+ T cell infiltration—yielding the phenotype that often mimics celiac disease. There are three pathogenic determinants that have been elucidated so far. First, almost absent mucosal IgA is permeating and facilitating gut pathogen expansion. With this process, gut membrane lipid metabolism is shifted toward inflammatory cascades, which may render an inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-like phenotype. Second, a mixed and specific type I/III and type II interferon release drives CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity and macrophage recruitment, producing a graft-versus-host-like mucosal damage pattern yielding apparent villous injury. Third, chronic norovirus infection further augments this interferon-driven pathway, leading to high-grade epithelial damage even in early-onset disease. USIDNET registry analysis (n = 1,415) confirmed that CVID-E patients exhibit significantly lower performance status, higher rates of concomitant autoimmunity (30.7%), granulomatous disease, and even malignancy. Treatment is largely empirical with limited evidence-based data. Immunoglobulin replacement does not mitigate symptoms of enteropathy, and although corticosteroids restore architecture, they impose prohibitive infectious risk. Although TNF-α blockers and thiopurines achieved complete remission in select patient cohorts, overall therapeutic response was unsatisfying. Molecular medical tactics—employing JAK inhibitors targeting the interferon-specific pathways, namely abatacept for CTLA-4-related dysregulation—represent the most promising tool. CVID-E is a complicated disorder because it stands at the very intersection of immunodeficiency, immune dysregulation, and mucosal pathology where these determinants encompass collapsed humoral defense, gut dysbiosis, and unbalanced interferon-driven epithelial necrosis converge. Multicenter randomized controlled trials and precision therapeutics are urgently needed to supersede the current empirical interventions with a fully evidence-based approach.
papers.abstract_zh: 常见变异型免疫缺陷(CVID),作为最常见的症状性原发性抗体缺陷(约1:25,000),其症状谱远超难以治愈、慢性且反复发作的感染。非感染性肠病(CVID-E)影响约15–30%的患者,已成为自然疾病进程中的关键表现,其风险约为11倍。CVID-E的病理特征由绒毛萎缩、缺乏黏膜浆细胞以及大量CD8+ T细胞浸润所决定,这种表型常与乳糜泻相似。目前已阐明三种致病机制。首先,几乎缺失的黏膜IgA会渗透并促进肠道病原体的扩增。在此过程中,肠道膜脂质代谢向炎症级联反应转移,可能导致类似炎症性肠病(IBD)的表型。其次,一种混合且特异性的I型/III型和II型干扰素释放驱动CD8+ T细胞的细胞毒性作用和巨噬细胞募集,产生类似移植物抗宿主病(GVHD)的黏膜损伤模式,导致明显的绒毛损伤。第三,慢性诺如病毒感染进一步增强这种干扰素驱动的通路,即使在早发性疾病中也会导致严重的上皮损伤。USIDNET注册分析(n = 1,415)证实,CVID-E患者表现出显著较低的生存状态,同时并发自身免疫(30.7%)、肉芽肿性疾病甚至恶性肿瘤的发病率更高。治疗的治疗主要基于经验,缺乏基于证据的数据。免疫球蛋白替代治疗无法缓解肠病症状,尽管糖皮质激素能够恢复肠道结构,但会带来显著的感染风险。尽管TNF-α阻断剂和硫嘌呤类药物在某些患者队列研究中实现了完全缓解,但总体治疗效果仍不令人满意。分子医学策略——使用针对干扰素特异性通路的JAK抑制剂,例如用于CTLA-4相关失调的阿巴西普——代表了最有前景的治疗工具。CVID-E是一种复杂的疾病,因为它处于免疫缺陷、免疫失调和黏膜病理的交汇点,这些致病因素包括体液免疫防御崩溃、肠道菌群失调以及干扰素驱动的上皮坏死失衡。亟需多中心随机对照试验和精准治疗来取代当前的经验性干预,以实现基于充分证据的治疗方案。

PLOS Clim 5(8): e0001040. https://doi. org/10.1371/journal.pclm.0001040 Editor: Jamie Males, PLOS Climate, UNITED KINGDOM OF GREAT BRITAIN AND NORTHERN IRELAND Published: August 21, 2026 Copyright: © 2026 Tang et al.
