Ben & Jerry's owner Magnum releases H1 2026 financial report by Timothy McQuiston, Vermont Business Magazine The Magnum Ice Cream Company Inc, the owner of Vermont-based Ben & Jerry's Homemade, among other well-known brands, and the largest ice cream-only company in the world, on July 30, 2026, reported their first half 2026 financial results. The Dutch firm reported an increase in sales and profits. Vermont establishes state’s first dedicated tourism brand Vermont Business Magazine The State of Vermont has launched its first dedicated tourism brand under the new positioning, “State of Inspiration,” designed to increase visitor intent and strengthen the state’s visibility in one of the most competitive tourism regions in the United States. The new brand responds to a paradox uncovered in the state's 2025 research program Graff: Ralph Wright, his brother’s keeper by Chris Graff As the 1985 General Assembly convened, Rep. Robert Kinsey, R-Craftsbury, was confident that he would be elected speaker of the House. He needed 76 votes to win, the Republicans held a 78-72 majority, and his latest count of pledges gave him a nice cushion of 80 votes. UVM Health job eliminations impact 142 total positions Vermont Business Magazine University of Vermont Health today informed employees that 142 positions have been eliminated. Of those, 76 positions have been permanently eliminated, and 66 will be posted as new roles with restructured job descriptions. Ski Vermont reports strongest skier visits since 2014-15 Vermont Business Magazine Ski Vermont capped the 2025-26 ski season at its 57th Annual Meeting at Jay Peak Resort today, highlighting a winter of favorable weather, strong visitation, and continued improvements at Vermont ski areas. Partners, supporters, and friends of the industry joined Ski Vermont’s alpine and cross-country members to reflect on a successful season. 1 2 3 4 5 6 PreviousNext -A +A Current News DFR launches campaign to help Vermonters understand health insurance coverage Tue, 08/25/2026 - 16:38 by tim Vermont Business Magazine The Vermont Department of Financial Regulation (DFR) is launching a new campaign aimed at helping Vermonters better understand state and federal laws requiring health insurance coverage of reproductive, preventive, and telehealth services and how to file complaints for incorrect coverage. The campaign and new webpage provide clear, actionable information for Vermonters with state-regulated commercial health insurance about services that are required to be covered by state and federal laws, often at low or no cost. These include preventive and contraceptive services, including a 12-month supply of prescription birth control, other FDA-approved contraceptives, and related services such as counseling, procedures, and follow-up visits. read more Pieciak reminds Vermonters to apply for Invest in Vermont funding by September 4 Tue, 08/25/2026 - 15:10 by tim Vermont Business Magazine Vermont housing developers, nonprofits, instrumentalities of the state, and other eligible organizations have until September 4 to apply for funding through Treasurer Mike Pieciak’s Invest in Vermont program. The treasurer announced in July that an additional $25 million is available through the program for projects supporting housing, job creation, and affordability across Vermont. The new funding builds on more than $130 million already awarded through Invest in Vermont by the treasurer. Collectively, those investments have leveraged over a half a billion dollars of outside capital, supporting nearly 1,700 units of affordable, high-quality housing and 200 permanent jobs—all without raising taxes. read more Join the SBA Vermont District Office at three events this week Tue, 08/25/2026 - 15:00 by tim Vermont Business Magazine Along with "Navy Week Burlington" on Wednesday, VMEC is teaming up with the U.S. Small Business Administration Vermont District Office on Thursday to bring you “VMEC 101 - Who We Are and Why We Exist.” This hour-long webinar will introduce you to Vermont’s only solely-focused manufacturing provider and partner. Whether you’ve attended a one-day public training, had one of our advisors on-site for a multi-day or many weeks project or have never heard of us, let us share with you the many ways that we can enhance your operation, from front office to factory floor and everything in between. Also on Thursday is the StartUp Rutland Small Business Mixer. read more Welch demands answers on DHS $464M no-bid contract to Trump-allied company for luxury jets Tue, 08/25/2026 - 12:47 by tim Vermont Business Magazine Today, U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vermont), Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, joined U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee in sending a letter demanding answers from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) about Department’s purchase of ten airplanes for $464 million via a no-bid contract to a company led by William Walters, a strong political ally of President Trump. In the letter to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, the Senators called out the Department’s reliance on no-bid contracts since the beginning of the second Trump Administration and raised concerns that the owner of the company that received the award also runs a company alleged to have solicited kickback payments from former DHS official Corey Lewandowski. read more Vermont Secretary of State statement on mail-in voting rules Tue, 08/25/2026 - 11:17 by tim Vermont Business Magazine Yesterday, the US Supreme Court issued a ruling that overturned one of the court orders blocking United States Postal Service (USPS) rules on mail-in voting from moving forward. The rule proposes complicated mailing requirements, and ballots would only be allowed to be mailed if the voter is on a federal list of approved voters. Another court order blocking the USPS rules from moving forward remains in place. Effectively, this means the State of Vermont’s plans for universal vote-by-mail remain unchanged. Additional litigation is expected to challenge the USPS’s rule-making efforts on this issue. read more VDH: COVID active but little health effect Tue, 08/25/2026 - 11:16 by tim by Timothy McQuiston, Vermont Business Magazine The Vermont Department of Health has reported have COVID-19 hospitalizations remain scarce and total levels are nearly too low to measure. They are at a similar level to the levels seen last summer. However, COVID remains active in Vermont and nationally. Meanwhile, Flu A and Flu B have essentially disappeared. There are still some samples showing Norovirus and RSV showing up in Vermont. read more State is 10th highest in healthcare cost-to-income Tue, 08/25/2026 - 11:05 by tim Vermont Business Magazine The relative weight of healthcare expenditure varies dramatically across the country, equaling more than twice as much income in the highest-ranked state as in the lowest. Researchers at MediFind ranked all 50 states by combining per-capita expenditure on hospitals, physician and clinical services, dental care, and prescription drugs. The total was then measured against median income to show where healthcare expenditure represents the greatest economic burden. Vermont ranked 10th highest at 13.11%. Hospital services were the largest of four categories at $5,638 out of an annual $9,497 total against income of $72,461. read more Vermont records seventh highest rate of cervical cancer deaths in the U.S. Tue, 08/25/2026 - 10:52 by tim Vermont Business Magazine A new 50-state analysis of federal health data released in August has found that Vermont has the 7th highest cervical cancer death rate in the nation. From 2020 to 2024, Vermont recorded 33.9 cervical cancer deaths per 100,000 female residents, more than 2 times higher than Massachusetts, the lowest-ranked state at 13.9 deaths per 100,000, though with limited data and small sample size. During the five-year study period, approximately 21,100 women across 49 states died from cervical cancer, with Vermont’s rate standing significantly above the national average. read more 1 in 5 Vermont homes is vacant, 2nd highest rate in the U.S. Tue, 08/25/2026 - 10:32 by tim Vermont Business Magazine The U.S. has far more vacant homes than many might expect. In fact, 14.5 million U.S. homes — roughly 1 in 10 nationwide — are empty. Vermont ranks as second highest (one in five homes), as tourist-destination states generally have high vacancy rates. But vacancy doesn’t always mean availability. Some empty units are used seasonally, while others are available for rent — and fewer than 800,000 are listed for sale. In Vermont, 75.8% of vacant homes are seasonal or recreational properties. As a result, 14.7% of the state’s housing units are empty during the offseason. In the District of Columbia, meanwhile, the largest share of vacancies is tied to the rental market. Homes available for rent make up 39.4% of the district’s vacant units — the highest such share in the nation — representing 4.0% of all housing units. read more Study reveals widespread use of problematic epistemologies in LLMs and Agentic AI Tue, 08/25/2026 - 10:07 by tim Vermont Business Magazine Woodstock-based Artificial Epistemics, LLC (AE) announced today its initial findings from an ongoing study of prevailing epistemologies (knowledge production functions) in leading large language models (LLMs) and Agentic AIs (AAIs). Using a distinction philosophers make between justificationist and falsificationist approaches, the AE team found that virtually all LLMs/AAIs at least implicitly rely on justificationist thinking when formulating responses to prompts. Any reliance upon allegedly 'established', 'authoritative', 'consensus-based', or "verified" knowledge is, in epistemological terms, notoriously fallacious, since the rank or status of individuals, groups, or majorities has nothing to do with the truth or legitimacy of the claims they make. Their claims, too, are fallible. read more Fidium earns top internet performance rankings in latest Speedtest analysis Tue, 08/25/2026 - 08:07 by tim Vermont Business Magazine Fidium, Vermont's leading fiber internet and network services provider connecting people, businesses and communities with its 100% fiber-to-the-premise network, today announced that it has earned top performance rankings for the state in Ookla’s analysis of Q1-Q2 2026 Speedtest Intelligence data. Based on consumer-initiated testing, these results demonstrate Fidium's strength across download speed, upload speed, responsiveness, reliability and gaming experience. read more UVM's Larner College of Medicine welcomes medical class of 2030 Tue, 08/25/2026 - 06:50 by tim by Stephanie Knific, UVM For 124 new medical students, Orientation Week marked the beginning of their journey at the Larner College of Medicine. From August 10-14, Larner welcomed its 203rd medical class with a week of activities designed to build community, introduce students to the college's learning environment, and familiarize them with the academic programs, resources, faculty, staff, and classmates who will shape their medical school experience. read more Pagination Current page 1 Page 2 Page 3 Page 4 Page 5 Page 6 Page 7 Page 8 Page 9 ... news.content_title: Over a dozen sickened in fourth gastrointestinal illness outbreak on cruise ship in two months
news.content: Over a dozen people were sickened with gastrointestinal illness on a National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions cruise in the vessel’s fourth outbreak in a less than two-month period, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . Eight of the 57 guests and five crew members on board National Geographic Sea Bird reported feeling ill during its July 15 voyage, the CDC said. Their main symptoms were reported to be abdominal cramps, vomiting and diarrhea. The cause of the illness is currently unknown, the CDC said. In response to this gastrointestinal illness outbreak, Lindblad Expeditions and crew aboard the ship increased cleaning and disinfection procedures, isolated the ill passengers and crew, consulted with Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) about sanitation cleaning procedures and reporting ill cases, and paused passenger operations. Lindblad told USA TODAY in an emailed statement that it canceled three voyages scheduled to embark on July 20, July 25 and July 30 “to conduct enhanced sanitation protocols aligned with the highest industry standards and provide additional time to help prevent the risk of further cases.” “We are working directly with affected guests to provide refunds, support and alternative travel arrangements,” the company added. The ship is currently en route to Ketchikan, Alaska, according to CruiseMapper.com . These new gastrointestinal illness cases follow three other outbreaks on the ship since late May. The first two were caused by norovirus while the third remains unknown, the CDC said. Outbreak of diarrhea-causing parasite expands to 4 more states Gastrointestinal illness (GI) is a common term for acute gastroenteritis (AGE), which has symptoms described as vomiting along with one of the following symptoms: diarrhea, muscle aches, headache, abdominal cramps or fever. Cruise ships are required to report these cases to the CDC. Norovirus is often a cause of gastrointestinal illness outbreaks on cruise ships, but the cause is not often found until an investigation has been completed. The CDC reported nine outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness on cruise ships that met the threshold for public notification so far this year. Norovirus was listed as the cause of five, and two others were caused by E.coli. The rest are still unknown. Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. All rights reserved. news.content: News Space Sports Restaurants Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals DINING What's a foodborne illness? And how can you avoid the ick and sick? Lyn Dowling For FLORIDA TODAY Aug. 21, 2026, 5:03 a.m. ET How many times have you heard it? “I’m not going to that restaurant again. The food there made me sick.” Or perhaps one of the many customers or workers in the place already was sick and passed it on, or that you weren’t quite sanitary enough about the way you washed before you handled your food and/or beverages. We certainly have precautions. Representatives of Florida’s Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR) reported that, as of the beginning of August, they have inspected 65,397 restaurants throughout the state this year (nearly 100,000 in the past decade), all with a mind toward keeping Floridians and visitors happy, healthy diners. We think about such thing as summer winds down and the last great cookout, on the Labor Day weekend, is just about ready to go, while eateries exit what some call the “summer slump” and head toward the year-end holidays. And while chances are very good indeed that you won’t be laid low, it is wise to take due care when it comes to foodborne illnesses, other than avoiding products of named growers or distributors caught up in the lettuce-and-jalapenos outbreak of this summer. Food-related illnesses were there before the outbreak became known and will be there after it is long gone. They tend to spike on hot, summer holiday weekends, so if you really think food is to blame for your misery, take it seriously, doctors say. “Everybody thinks about a foodborne illness as (simply) gastroenteritis, but it’s not just that,” said Health First-affiliated Dr. Gary Hardoon, who practices internal medicine in Palm Bay and Rockledge. “It is a virus, a bacteria or a parasite, depending on what you’ve (contracted), though the main ones are bacterial and viral. Salmonella really is one of the biggest bacterial causes, about a million patients per year, and norovirus is the most common virus among patients.” Every year, millions of us will face a foodborne illness Statistics from the Centers for Disease Control bear out Hardoon’s words, not least the part about taking it seriously: About 48 million people get sick from a foodborne illness each year. Of those, 128,000 are hospitalized and 3,000 die. Norovirus tops all foodborne germs, statistics about which Hardoon can recite. “It is the most common, and it just smacks me when I look at restaurant inspections that the most basic things are most important: sanitation, care in handling, cleanliness,” he said. So, what should diners be on the lookout for if they think they may be at risk for foodborne illness? Well, there are the classic symptoms, Hardoon said, and none is, “I just didn’t like the way that tasted. “Frequent vomiting, six or more runny bowel movements, severe abdominal pain, high fever,” he said. “Every one has a different incubation period.” And related to precautions: “The biggest thing is dehydration,” he added. “Usually, you don’t use much care in hydrating yourself more than the norm, but if you start to feel ill and start to see complications, dehydration can be a cause. So the most important thing is staying well hydrated, especially with any electrolyte-rich fluid.” The rest goes where it should: If you’re sick, see a doctor. Looking forward to ooky-spooky fun? Make plans now Let’s hear it for Ford’s Garage, which had the wisdom to announce its annual Trunk or Treat Halloween event early. It will take place from 5 to 9 p.m. Oct. 29 at the restaurant, 5480 Lake Andrew Drive, Viera, with trick-or-treating, axe throwing, face painting, a kids’ costume contest, and best decorated trunk/golf cart awards as well as, you guessed it, candy. Vehicle registration is free and may be accomplished at https://forms.gle/KMZr1nSgqfqteLCp9. There’s also Cadillac Cove, which will offer more than $1,000 in costume prizes the very night of Halloween, Oct. 31. Festivities start at 8 p.m., will continue through midnight with live music by the Mixtape Kids and are open to people 21 years old and older. Cadillac Cove is located at 1462 S.R. A1A, Satellite Beach. Visit https://cadillaccovebeachside.com. Friends, if you want attention for your autumnal or fall holiday events, write lyndowling@yahoo.com. news.content_original: News Space Sports Restaurants Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals DINING What's a foodborne illness? And how can you avoid the ick and sick? Lyn Dowling For FLORIDA TODAY Aug. 21, 2026, 5:03 a.m. ET How many times have you heard it? “I’m not going to that restaurant again. The food there made me sick.” Or perhaps one of the many customers or workers in the place already was sick and passed it on, or that you weren’t quite sanitary enough about the way you washed before you handled your food and/or beverages. We certainly have precautions. Representatives of Florida’s Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR) reported that, as of the beginning of August, they have inspected 65,397 restaurants throughout the state this year (nearly 100,000 in the past decade), all with a mind toward keeping Floridians and visitors happy, healthy diners. We think about such thing as summer winds down and the last great cookout, on the Labor Day weekend, is just about ready to go, while eateries exit what some call the “summer slump” and head toward the year-end holidays. And while chances are very good indeed that you won’t be laid low, it is wise to take due care when it comes to foodborne illnesses, other than avoiding products of named growers or distributors caught up in the lettuce-and-jalapenos outbreak of this summer. Food-related illnesses were there before the outbreak became known and will be there after it is long gone. They tend to spike on hot, summer holiday weekends, so if you really think food is to blame for your misery, take it seriously, doctors say. “Everybody thinks about a foodborne illness as (simply) gastroenteritis, but it’s not just that,” said Health First-affiliated Dr. Gary Hardoon, who practices internal medicine in Palm Bay and Rockledge. “It is a virus, a bacteria or a parasite, depending on what you’ve (contracted), though the main ones are bacterial and viral. Salmonella really is one of the biggest bacterial causes, about a million patients per year, and norovirus is the most common virus among patients.” Every year, millions of us will face a foodborne illness Statistics from the Centers for Disease Control bear out Hardoon’s words, not least the part about taking it seriously: About 48 million people get sick from a foodborne illness each year. Of those, 128,000 are hospitalized and 3,000 die. Norovirus tops all foodborne germs, statistics about which Hardoon can recite. “It is the most common, and it just smacks me when I look at restaurant inspections that the most basic things are most important: sanitation, care in handling, cleanliness,” he said. So, what should diners be on the lookout for if they think they may be at risk for foodborne illness? Well, there are the classic symptoms, Hardoon said, and none is, “I just didn’t like the way that tasted. “Frequent vomiting, six or more runny bowel movements, severe abdominal pain, high fever,” he said. “Every one has a different incubation period.” And related to precautions: “The biggest thing is dehydration,” he added. “Usually, you don’t use much care in hydrating yourself more than the norm, but if you start to feel ill and start to see complications, dehydration can be a cause. So the most important thing is staying well hydrated, especially with any electrolyte-rich fluid.” The rest goes where it should: If you’re sick, see a doctor. Looking forward to ooky-spooky fun? Make plans now Let’s hear it for Ford’s Garage, which had the wisdom to announce its annual Trunk or Treat Halloween event early. It will take place from 5 to 9 p.m. Oct. 29 at the restaurant, 5480 Lake Andrew Drive, Viera, with trick-or-treating, axe throwing, face painting, a kids’ costume contest, and best decorated trunk/golf cart awards as well as, you guessed it, candy. Vehicle registration is free and may be accomplished at https://forms.gle/KMZr1nSgqfqteLCp9. There’s also Cadillac Cove, which will offer more than $1,000 in costume prizes the very night of Halloween, Oct. 31. Festivities start at 8 p.m., will continue through midnight with live music by the Mixtape Kids and are open to people 21 years old and older. Cadillac Cove is located at 1462 S.R. A1A, Satellite Beach. Visit https://cadillaccovebeachside.com. Friends, if you want attention for your autumnal or fall holiday events, write lyndowling@yahoo.com.
